subject: Request: Ramp-control & customer note for FastPay latency spike
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Brendan Cole <brendan@fastpay.io>
Cc: FastPay Oncall <oncall@fastpay.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Ramp-control & customer note for FastPay latency spike

Team —

We’re seeing a sustained p99 latency increase for FastPay starting ~08:45 PDT. Key signals: 4x queue depth on the inference pool serving fp-payments-v1, p95 jumped from 220ms -> ~950ms and p99 into the 2.4s range, and client-side retries are increasing. Customer (Brendan) has flagged rising errors on their end.

Immediate asks:
- Can SRE/Infra apply a short-term ramp-control (traffic shaping) on incoming FastPay requests for the next 60–90 minutes while we stabilize? We want to reduce burstiness rather than full cutover.
- Engineering: can we enable fallback routing to the quantized fp-payments-v1-q variant (same semantics, lower perf but higher concurrency) if pool queue depth > 300?
- CS/Account: I need a short customer-facing note we can send to FastPay in the next 30–45 minutes — draft attached (draft-customer-note.md).

Attached I’m adding a CSV export of p99 by shard and a screenshot of queue depth. Please confirm ownership of each item and ETA. If we can’t get routing enabled quickly, we should plan an explicit reduced-rate window to avoid client-side retries escalating.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Brendan Cole <brendan@fastpay.io>
Cc: FastPay Oncall <oncall@fastpay.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Ramp-control & customer note for FastPay latency spike

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 09:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> We’re seeing a sustained p99 latency increase for FastPay starting ~08:45 PDT...

Quick triage: I’ve looked at the pool logs and allocation telemetry. Short summary:
- Root proximate cause looks like autoscaler lag combined with heavier-than-usual long-context requests from one customer shard. The batching distribution shifted (more long sequences) and our usual continuous batcher is producing larger batches that starve latency-sensitive requests.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~18% for that model (likely different prompt prefixes in new test traffic).

Immediate mitigations I can push in ~20–30 minutes:
1) Increase active workers in the fp-payments-v1 pool by +2 replicas (hot swap) — reduces queue depth.
2) Temporarily force conservative batching (max batch size 32 -> 16) for the pool; trades throughput for predictable latency.
3) Enable routing rule to send new requests from FastPay to fp-payments-v1-q when queue depth > 300 (I can add the rule and test).

If SRE can apply a client-facing ramp-control signal (token-bucket or 429 shaping) that would give us the breathing room to apply 1–3 safely. Attaching p99-compare.csv and screenshot-queue-depth.png for reference.

Dev Patel
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Brendan Cole <brendan@fastpay.io>
Cc: FastPay Oncall <oncall@fastpay.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Ramp-control & customer note for FastPay latency spike

Thanks Dev — I agree with the short-term plan. A couple of product/ops notes:
- Ramp-control approach: prefer shaping -> allow 60% of historical baseline traffic for 30 minutes, then re-evaluate. Full throttle-down risks client retries that will just push bursts back.
- Fallback variant: fp-payments-v1-q is fine as short-term; watch model differences closely (tokenization edge cases). We should set an automatic guardrail to route back once p95 < 350ms for 10 minutes.
- Credits/SLA: if this becomes >60 minutes of degraded p99, Customer Success (Marissa) and I will need to agree on a remediation credit; flagging this for finance.

Proposed customer note bullets (sendable after we confirm ramp-control in place, I can edit for tone):
> - We observed increased latency on our inference service affecting a subset of FastPay requests.
> - We applied temporary traffic shaping to protect request reliability while we applied server-side mitigations (worker scale and conservative batching).
> - We've enabled a fallback model variant to reduce queuing and expect shorter latencies within ~30 minutes.
> - We'll provide a follow-up when systems return to baseline and include an incident summary.

I’ll create INF-4321 and link the runbook; please add any specifics. Marissa — can you own the external send after Vanessa signs off?

Karthik Iyer
Head of SRE | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Brendan Cole <brendan@fastpay.io>, FastPay Oncall <oncall@fastpay.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Ramp-control & customer note for FastPay latency spike

Thanks all — short status and action items.

Status (16:08 PDT):
- SRE has applied a 60% traffic shaping policy for FastPay (applies at edge token-bucket) as of 15:50 PDT.
- Dev increased pool workers and forced conservative batching at 15:58 PDT.
- Routing rule to fp-payments-v1-q enabled at 16:02 PDT when queue depth > 300.
- Observed p99 trending down — currently ~480ms and improving.

Action items / ownership:
- Marissa: please send the customer-facing note below to Brendan and the FastPay oncall alias now. I’ve attached a draft (draft-customer-note.md).
- Karthik & Dev: continue monitoring INF-4321 and post a short incident summary by EOD.
- Stephanie: coordinate with finance if p99 stays degraded >60 minutes for remediation credits.

Draft customer note (Marissa — please paste with our header):

Subject: Update: Temporary traffic shaping and mitigation steps — Redwood inference

Brendan / FastPay team —

We identified an increase in inference latency affecting a subset of your requests this morning. To preserve availability, we applied temporary traffic shaping while we scaled additional workers and enabled a fallback model variant. We expect latency to return to baseline within the hour and will follow up with a short incident report.

If you see any residual errors or need us to pause traffic for a controlled window, reply to this thread and we’ll coordinate immediately.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re focused on preventing recurrence.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-customer-note.md, p99-compare.csv, screenshot-queue-depth.png

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
